title: Easy2U user manual
text: Easy2U user manual English internal edition · 25 September 2026. These instructions and screenshots were checked against the current source and a local release build with synthetic accounts. Live camera and assessment recovery, institution support details, and first-time reader testing require further review before public distribution. Choose the guide for your role: - — join a class, take or recover a quiz, see results, and create personal practice quizzes. - — create classes and quizzes, publish, review attempts, release results, and export reports. - — fast recovery steps when a student is paused or cannot submit. - — find a symptom and its next step. - — meanings of assessment, reveal, attempt, and other labels. - — what to report and who can resolve it.

title: Using the manual on a phone
text: Using the manual on a phone Easy2U uses top navigation on a desktop and a bottom dock on a phone. Some lecturer tools use sheets or compact lists on a phone. The guides label steps Desktop and Phone wherever the action changes. Close the on-screen keyboard if the bottom dock is temporarily hidden.

title: Before you start
text: Before you start Use the account and class details supplied by your institution or lecturer. Assessments that require face verification need a working camera, camera permission, and a well-lit space. Some options, including Microsoft sign-in, AI question generation, web topic search, and hand gestures, appear only when your institution or lecturer enables them. This searchable website is the primary manual. for printing or offline use. It is generated from the same content. See the for the app version and capture date.

title: Student guide
text: Student guide Use this guide for class assessments and personal practice. A class quiz is assigned by a lecturer and may be a practice quiz or an assessment. A personal quiz is yours to create and practice; it is not class work and does not produce a class grade. A class quiz marked Live is available subject to its schedule and attempt rules. Draft quizzes are not available to students; Closed quizzes cannot be started.

title: Create an account or sign in
text: Create an account or sign in Where to go: Open your institution's Easy2U address and choose Create account or Sign in . You need internet access and an email address. Use an institutional Microsoft account only if that option is offered by your institution.

title: Create a student account
text: Create a student account 1. Open Create account . 2. Enter your Full name , Email address , and Password . The form requires a password of at least six characters. 3. Under I am a… , choose Student and enter your Matric number . The form describes the expected matric format. 4. Read Biometric Consent , including its notice that camera/microphone footage before an integrity incident may be recorded and reviewed. Select I understand and consent to face verification for assessments only if you agree. This account consent is required to create an account; face capture is a separate step described below. 5. Select Create account . If the app asks you to confirm your email, follow the email instructions, then return to Sign in . Otherwise, the app signs you in and opens My Classes . What happens next: Your account's student role opens the student area. If you arrived through a class QR code, t

title: Sign in, reset a password, or sign out
text: Sign in, reset a password, or sign out 1. Open Sign in and enter Email address and Password . 2. If your institution offers a Microsoft sign-in option, select it and complete the provider's prompts. This option is institution-dependent and may not appear. 3. If a matric capture prompt appears for your institutional account, enter the matric number requested and submit it once. This is an account setup step; the application returns you to the page you were trying to open when possible. 4. To reset a forgotten password, select Forgot password? , enter your email, and select Send reset link . Open the message sent to that address and use its link to set a new password. The confirmation message is generic whether or not an account exists. 5. To sign out, open the account menu and choose Sign out . What happens next: A successful student sign-in opens My Classes , unless you followed a QR/sha

title: Find your way around
text: Find your way around Desktop — different navigation. Use the top navigation: My Classes , Class Quizzes , My Quizzes , and Face Setup . Open the account control to see account information and Sign out . The bell opens notifications; its badge shows how many are unread. Select a notification to open its related page and mark it read, or select Mark all as read . The language control switches between EN and BM . The theme control cycles through Light , Dark , and System . Phone — different navigation. Use the bottom navigation to open My Classes , Class Quizzes , My Quizzes , or Face Setup . The header keeps the brand, notification bell, and account avatar; select the avatar for the account sheet. Language and theme controls are in that sheet and work the same way as on desktop. The notification badge shows unread items; opening a notification marks it read. On phones, the bottom navigatio

title: Join a class
text: Join a class Where to go: Sign in, then open My Classes . Get the six-character join code or class QR from your lecturer. You must be signed in as a student. Desktop: select a class card to open its quizzes, or use Join a class to enter a code. Select the image to enlarge it.

title: Join with a code
text: Join with a code 1. Desktop: Select Join a class on the classes page. Phone: Select the floating Join a class control on My Classes ; it opens a bottom drawer. If you have not joined any class yet, select Enter a join code . 2. Enter the six-character code in Join code . The entry accepts uppercase letters and numbers; codes exclude ambiguous characters. 3. Select Join class . Desktop: enter the six characters in the join dialog, then select Join class. Select the image to enlarge it. Phone: the same code entry opens in a bottom drawer. Select the image to enlarge it. What happens next: A success notice names the class, and the class appears under My Classes . Selecting its class card opens the class-filtered quiz list.

title: Join from a QR code
text: Join from a QR code 1. Scan the QR code your lecturer provides with your phone camera. The code opens the class confirmation page. 2. If asked, sign in or create a student account. The app returns to the pending join confirmation. 3. Check the class join code shown on screen, then select Join class . What happens next: The app confirms the join and returns to My Classes . Scanning alone does not join you; confirm the action on the page. If it does not work: Check all six characters with your lecturer. A code may be invalid or for an archived class; repeated incorrect attempts may temporarily lock joining. If you already joined, the app reports that state. See .

title: Find a class quiz
text: Find a class quiz Where to go: Open Class Quizzes . To focus on one class, select its card from My Classes ; the quiz list is then filtered to that class. A quiz must be live and within its availability window. Class quiz cards identify the mode and show the available action or current status. Select the image to enlarge it. 1. Find the quiz by its title. Read its mode, due/deadline information if shown, time limit, and attempt status before starting. 2. Treat Practice as practice feedback and Assessment as graded class work. Correct answers may be hidden for an assessment until the lecturer releases results. 3. If the quiz is scheduled, wait until its opening time. If it is closed or the deadline has passed, contact the lecturer about availability. 4. Select Start to begin, or use the available resume/retake action shown on the quiz card. Retakes appear only when the lecturer has allowe

title: Set up face verification
text: Set up face verification Where to go: Open Face Setup from the top or bottom navigation, or select Enroll your face on the class quiz page. Some assessments require face verification; your lecturer or institution may configure different checks. Read the consent information before deciding whether to grant face verification consent. The camera stays off until you consent. Select the image to enlarge it. 1. Read Biometric Consent . Select I understand and consent to face verification for assessments only if you agree to the described camera and face processing. The camera remains off until you grant consent. 2. Allow camera access when your browser asks. Use a working front-facing camera in a well-lit place. Close other apps or tabs using the camera. 3. Center one face in the guide. Follow the on-screen instruction to blink and turn your head to the front, left, and right positions. Wait f

title: Take and submit an assessment
text: Take and submit an assessment Where to go: Open Class Quizzes , choose a live Assessment , and select Start . Read the instructions before beginning. A camera/liveness check or fullscreen prompt may appear depending on the quiz and institution settings. Desktop answer controls: this practice example shows the question, answer cards, progress, and Skip this question. An assessment may add a face gate and timer. Select the image to enlarge it. Phone answer controls: answer cards stack vertically, and Quiz Info appears above progress. This is a practice example; an assessment may add checks. Select the image to enlarge it. 1. At the assessment gate, allow camera access if asked. Center your face and follow the blink instruction. If the app asks for fullscreen, accept the browser prompt. Select Begin assessment when it becomes available. 2. Read the question and its answer format. For a sing

title: Recover during a quiz
text: Recover during a quiz Where to go: Stay on the quiz page and read the pause or warning overlay. A temporary pause is a protection/recovery state and does not by itself mean your attempt was flagged. 1. Follow the message on the overlay. If it asks you to verify your face, center your face and blink when prompted. 2. If the camera stopped, restore the browser's camera permission, close any other app using the camera, and use the displayed retry/recovery action. 3. If the page lost focus or fullscreen, return to the quiz tab and re-enter fullscreen if prompted. 4. If the overlay says to wait for your lecturer to unlock the attempt, contact the lecturer and give them the quiz title and approximate time of the pause. Do not start a second attempt unless the quiz card explicitly offers a retake. 5. When the player resumes, check the question and timer. The app may save answers as you go, but

title: See your results
text: See your results Where to go: Open Class Quizzes and find the completed quiz. 1. If the card says Awaiting results , the lecturer has not revealed the result. You cannot open a score yet; check later or contact the lecturer if the release date has passed. 2. After release, select View results on the quiz card. The player results screen shows your score and, when enabled, question review/feedback. 3. For practice quizzes, feedback may appear immediately after completion. Use the review displayed by the player. Phone: Use Class Quizzes in the bottom navigation. The same Awaiting results and View results states are available in the compact list. What happens next: The result remains available from the quiz card while the quiz and account remain available. If it does not work: If the result is still awaiting release, ask your lecturer when it will be available. If the quiz is missing, check

title: Make a personal practice quiz
text: Make a personal practice quiz Where to go: Open My Quizzes . Personal quizzes belong to your account and are for practice; they do not count as class assessment results. Your personal practice quizzes appear under My Practice Quizzes. Select the image to enlarge it. 1. Select Create quiz , enter a Title , then select Create quiz again to make the quiz. 2. In the editor, enter the question prompt and answer choices or response details for the question type shown. Choose the correct answer when that option is provided. 3. Select Add this question . Repeat for more questions. Use the editor's controls to edit, reorder, or delete questions; attach an image only if the image control is available. 4. If AI question generation is offered, review every generated question and answer before using it. Availability depends on institution configuration. 5. Return to the quiz list and select Start or

title: Share or stop sharing a personal quiz
text: Share or stop sharing a personal quiz Where to go: Open My Quizzes and choose Share on the quiz you own. 1. Copy the displayed share link and send it to the intended recipient yourself. Anyone with an active share code may be able to open the practice content; share it accordingly. 2. To invalidate the current link, select New code , then Confirm . Give recipients the new link. The old link becomes unavailable. 3. To stop sharing, select Stop sharing . The old link becomes unavailable. A recipient already playing may lose access to questions/feedback as the quiz is unshared. 4. A recipient opens the shared link. If prompted, they sign in or create an account, then reopen the link and select Start practice . Phone: Open My Quizzes in the bottom navigation and use the quiz's Share action. The share dialog is responsive; follow the displayed controls. What happens next: A valid link opens t

title: Lecturer guide
text: Lecturer guide English internal edition. See the for the quick start and for common problems. This guide covers classes, quiz authoring, assessment monitoring, results, and reports. An institution may disable AI generation or web search. Those options appear here only when they are available in your account.

title: Sign in as a lecturer
text: Sign in as a lecturer You need: a lecturer account, or a lecturer invite code supplied by your institution. A student account does not gain lecturer access by changing its profile. 1. On Sign in , enter your Email address and Password , then select Sign in . If your institution offers it, you can select Sign in with Microsoft instead. 2. To make a new lecturer account, select Create one now , enter your name, email and password, select Lecturer under I am a… , and enter the Lecturer invite code supplied by your administrator. 3. Select Create account . If the app asks you to confirm your email, open the confirmation message before signing in. What happens next: you reach your lecturer dashboard, starting at My Classes . If you are sent to the student area, with your role or invite code. If it does not work: select Forgot password? on the sign-in page, or use .

title: Find your way around
text: Find your way around Desktop: use My Classes and Quizzes in the top navigation. The notification bell and account menu are in the header. Phone: use the bottom dock for classes and quizzes. On My Classes , use New Class to create a class; the center Create control opens choices for a new class or quiz. Open the account sheet for language, theme and sign-out options. The dock can hide while the on-screen keyboard is open; close the keyboard to see it again. Desktop: use the top navigation. The Create a class form is on My Classes. Select the image to enlarge it. Phone: use New Class on this page or the center Create control in the bottom dock. Select the image to enlarge it. The Quizzes library shows quizzes from all of your classes, including quizzes in archived classes. Search by title there. Open a draft in the builder or select Results for a published quiz.

title: Create a class and invite students
text: Create a class and invite students You need: a lecturer account. A class gets its own six-character join code when you create it. 1. Open My Classes . 2. Desktop: in Create a class , enter a Class title and select Create class . Phone: select Create New class , enter the title in the sheet, and select Create class . 3. Open the new class card. Find its Class Join Code . 4. Select Copy join code to send the code through your usual course channel. For students in the room, select Show QR and let them scan it. A student who is signed out is sent through sign-in and then returns to the join confirmation. 5. Ask students to confirm the class name and join. Open the class Students tab or roster section to check enrollment. Phone class detail: the sample code illustrates where to find yours. Use Show QR for students in the room; switch to Students to inspect the roster. Select the image to enla

title: Review the class roster
text: Review the class roster 1. Open My Classes , then open the class. 2. Desktop: find the Students section or tab. Phone: select the Students tab to switch from class quizzes to the roster. 3. Check the student names and matric numbers shown there. For a large class, a notice may say only the first 100 students are listed; other enrolled students still count toward quizzes and exports. For a student who cannot join, confirm you shared this class's current code and that the class is active. The can be sent to them.

title: Archive or restore a class
text: Archive or restore a class Archiving hides a class from students and stops new joins while preserving quizzes, results and audit history. Restoring makes its live quizzes available again. Confirm with your institution before archiving a class still in use. 1. Open the class from My Classes and select Archive class . 2. Read Archive this class? , then select Archive class to confirm. 3. To restore it, open Archived classes , find the class, select Restore , and confirm Restore class . What happens next: the restored class returns to My Classes . If it had live quizzes, check their schedule and availability before telling students to resume.

title: Create a quiz
text: Create a quiz You need: an active class. Decide whether students need repeat practice with immediate feedback or a controlled assessment. 1. Open My Classes and choose the class. Select New Quiz or find Create a new quiz . From the Quizzes library, you can also start New quiz and choose a destination class. 2. Enter the Quiz title and choose Quiz mode : Practice permits repeat attempts and immediate feedback; Assessment uses controlled attempts and may require face verification. 3. For an assessment, set Time limit if needed. Leave No time limit when there is no countdown. 4. Optionally set Opens at and Closes at . The form labels these times in Malaysia time. The closing time must follow the opening time. 5. If appropriate, turn on Allow retakes and choose Max attempts . Review Shuffle question & option order and Hand gestures before publishing; those draft settings cannot be changed on

title: Add and edit questions
text: Add and edit questions 1. Open the draft quiz's builder and find Add question . Phone: use the builder's add-question control to open its sheet. 2. Select Question type : Multiple choice , True / False , Multiple select , or Short answer (AI-marked) . 3. Enter the Question prompt . For option-based questions, enter distinct options and mark the Correct answer or Correct answers . For a short answer, provide a clear Answer key / rubric for the marker. 4. Add an optional explanation or question image, then select Add this question . Review the new item in Questions . 5. Use Edit , Move up , Move down , or Delete on a draft question as needed. Phone: expand the compact question controls if the actions are not visible immediately. Desktop builder: choose the question type and correct answer, then enter the prompt and options. Select the image to enlarge it. Phone builder: Add question opens

title: Import several questions
text: Import several questions 1. In a draft builder, select Import questions . 2. Paste a pipe-separated Question list , or select Upload file for a .txt or .csv text file. 3. Follow the example in the dialog to mark the correct answer with . Check Preview and correct every line-level warning. 4. Select Import questions when the preview shows the intended items. Import adds to the existing draft. It does not replace it. The dialog shows the remaining slots up to the 30-question limit. If you need to change an imported item, use Edit in the builder.

title: Generate questions with AI, when available
text: Generate questions with AI, when available AI output is a draft. You are responsible for checking wording, answer keys, images and suitability for your class before publication. 1. In a draft builder, select Generate from file . Choose Upload Documents for supported files or Paste Notes for text. The dialog accepts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT, MD and supported image files; it shows the current per-file and total limits. 2. For an image or scanned PDF, choose the available Document Scanner . Select Read Files & Continue or Continue with Text and inspect the extracted content. If pages were missed, correct that before generating. 3. Choose the number of questions, difficulty, format and quiz language. Use Custom AI Focus & Directives for topic guidance. If offered, Add up-to-date web knowledge searches for extra material in addition to your upload or notes. 4. Choose Add to existing questions or

title: Duplicate a quiz
text: Duplicate a quiz 1. Open the quiz builder and select Duplicate . The action may be under More actions on a narrow screen. 2. Choose an active Destination class and select Duplicate . 3. Select Open draft to review the new copy before publishing it. The copy includes questions, settings and images, but does not copy student attempts or results. The destination cannot be an archived class.

title: Publish and manage a quiz
text: Publish and manage a quiz Only a draft with at least one question can be published. Publishing makes it live, but an opening time can still prevent students from starting yet. 1. In the draft builder, review every question and its answer key. Check Quiz settings , including mode, time limit, schedule, retakes, shuffling and hand gestures. 2. Select Publish quiz and wait for the Live status. 3. Open Results to monitor attempts. If you set an availability window, check its Opens at and Closes at values before sharing the quiz. Phone publishing: check the question list, then use Publish quiz at the bottom of the builder. Select the image to enlarge it. What happens next: enrolled students can see the live quiz. They can start only while it is open and they have an available attempt.

title: Change a live quiz's availability
text: Change a live quiz's availability Some live settings, including the availability window and retakes, can be managed after publication. Question text, answer keys, shuffling and the gesture setting are draft-only. Use Edit settings or the schedule control where the quiz shows it, save the permitted changes, and confirm what the student quiz card now says.

title: Close a quiz
text: Close a quiz Closing is one-way. Students cannot start new attempts or answer more questions; a student already taking it can still submit recorded work. You may have to decide whether to reveal existing results as part of closing. 1. Open the live quiz's builder or Results and select Close quiz . 2. Read Close this quiz? , including any warning about submitted students whose results remain hidden. 3. Choose Reveal first, then close if it is offered and you want students to see their results, or choose Close anyway to leave results hidden. What happens next: the status becomes Closed . You cannot return it to Live. Check if students are waiting for scores.

title: Review attempts and help students
text: Review attempts and help students Open the class quiz and select Results . The Quiz Results & Integrity page groups sessions as Completed , Flagged , Abandoned , or In progress . Select a student's row to inspect their session, answer breakdown, and Integrity timeline . An event is a signal to review in context; it is not by itself a final judgment about a student. Desktop: use the results table and row actions. Phone: use the compact status filters and open the student's detail or Session actions menu. Results: filter sessions, open a student's answers, and use Question insights for patterns across the class. Select the image to enlarge it.

title: Review a pending face enrollment
text: Review a pending face enrollment A panel on My Classes can list students whose face enrollment needs a decision. Until reviewed, they cannot start a verified assessment. 1. Open My Classes and find the face enrollments need review panel. 2. Check the student and class using your institution's normal identity process. Select Approve if the enrollment is correct, or Reject — ask to re-enroll if the student must capture again. 3. Tell the student the outcome through the usual class channel. If you cannot establish the student's identity, contact your institution's administrator before approving.

title: Unlock, exempt, or reset an attempt
text: Unlock, exempt, or reset an attempt These are different actions. Choose the least disruptive one that addresses the student's situation. Action Effect --- --- Unlock Lets a flagged student continue after your review. Face-exempt Stops face checks for this one attempt. You must record a reason. Reset Permanently deletes this attempt's answers, progress and integrity details. It permits the student to start again and cannot be undone. 1. On Results , find the student's session and read the status and Integrity timeline . 2. Open Session actions if the buttons are in a menu. Select Unlock , Face-exempt , or Reset as appropriate. 3. For Face-exempt , enter the required Reason . For Reset , read the confirmation carefully before completing it. 4. Refresh your view of the student's session, then tell the student what to do next. Do not tell them to start a second attempt unless the resulting s

title: Review and adjust a short-answer mark
text: Review and adjust a short-answer mark AI-marked short answers may show Pending , Needs review , or Marking failed . Inspect the student's answer and rubric before releasing results. 1. Open Results , select the student's session, and locate the short-answer question. 2. Compare the response, Rubric , and any AI rationale . Select Adjust mark when a correction is needed. 3. Choose the permitted New mark , enter a Reason , and save. If results were already released, follow the page's prompt to republish the corrected mark so students see the change.

title: Release and analyze results
text: Release and analyze results Assessment scores can be visible to lecturers before students see them. Students see a score and answer review only after the results are released. Practice quizzes give more immediate feedback. Some assessments can be set to release automatically once the completion conditions are met.

title: Reveal assessment results
text: Reveal assessment results 1. Open the assessment's Results page and check completed attempts and any Pending or Needs review marks. 2. Read the Results are hidden panel. Select Reveal to students when the results are ready, then confirm. 3. Check that the page says Results revealed . Students can then open their scores and answer breakdowns. Revealing is a one-way release. If you later correct a short-answer mark, follow the republish instruction on the student's session detail.

title: Inspect question insights
text: Inspect question insights On Results , open Question insights . Compare the per-question correct rate and option choices to find questions students struggled with. A highlight such as Only …% correct is a prompt to review the teaching or question wording, not a diagnosis on its own. The page will warn you if its analysis was truncated for a very large class.

title: Open and export the gradebook
text: Open and export the gradebook 1. Open My Classes , choose the class, and select Gradebook . 2. Desktop: scan the student-by-assessment table, then search, filter, or sort. Phone: scan the student list; select a student or quiz to open its bottom sheet. Only published assessments appear in the gradebook. 3. Select Export Excel to download the class workbook. Keep it in an institution-approved location because it contains student information. Desktop gradebook: compare assessment columns and student rows; Export Excel is above the table. Select the image to enlarge it. Phone gradebook: select a student in the list to open their assessment breakdown. Select the image to enlarge it. For one quiz, select Export Excel on that quiz's Results page. The quiz export and class gradebook export are different reports. An unrevealed marker means the lecturer can see the score while students cannot yet

title: Notifications and account
text: Notifications and account Use the notification bell for updates such as a student attempt, flagged session, or enrollment needing review. Open a notice to reach its relevant class or quiz. In the account menu, switch Language or Theme , or select Sign out . On a phone, these settings appear in the account sheet. For a missing control, a code that does not work, or a failed export, start with . If the issue persists, use .

title: During the quiz
text: During the quiz Keep the quiz page open and follow the message shown in the player. A pause is a recovery state; it does not by itself mean your attempt has been flagged. Use this quick card if a check interrupts an assessment. What you see What to do --- --- Face check paused or a blink prompt Keep your face in the camera frame and blink when asked. Wait for the check to recover before answering. Hands left the camera Show your hand in the camera view, then blink to continue. Return to the exam Select Return to the exam to bring the quiz back to the foreground. Keep it open while answering. Fullscreen was closed Select Return to the exam . The quiz should continue where you left off. Camera unavailable Restore camera permission for Easy2U in your browser, close other apps using the camera, then follow the player prompt. Assessment flagged or lecturer unlock required Wait for your lectur

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting Use the closest symptom below. Keep the quiz page open during an assessment problem when possible. For issues that need staff access, contact your lecturer first; see for what to include and where to escalate.

title: Account and sign-in
text: Account and sign-in

title: I cannot create an account
text: I cannot create an account Check that Email is valid, the password has at least six characters, a student role is selected, and the requested Matric number is filled in. The registration form requires the biometric consent checkbox before Create account is enabled. Read the consent information before selecting it. If a field is rejected, correct it and submit again. If the same error persists, contact your institution's account administrator.

title: The app says the email or password is invalid
text: The app says the email or password is invalid Check the spelling and sign-in method. If you use institutional Microsoft sign-in, choose that option when it is offered. Select Forgot password? to request a reset link, then check the email inbox and spam folder. The reset confirmation is generic by design. If you cannot access your email or the reset link has expired, contact the institution's account administrator.

title: I am asked for a matric number
text: I am asked for a matric number Complete the one-time matric capture prompt for your institutional account. If the value is rejected, check the institution's expected format and contact its account administrator. Do not create a second account to work around the prompt.

title: A QR join link sends me to sign in and I do not return to the class
text: A QR join link sends me to sign in and I do not return to the class Finish sign-in or registration in the same browser. Open the QR link again if necessary, review the displayed class code, then explicitly confirm the join. A QR scan only opens the confirmation page; it does not enroll you automatically.

title: Class joining
text: Class joining

title: The join code is rejected
text: The join code is rejected Check that it has six characters and compare it with the lecturer's current code. Codes can be invalid or for an archived class. If several incorrect attempts have triggered a temporary lock, wait for the lock to expire and ask the lecturer to confirm the code. Do not keep guessing.

title: The app says I already joined
text: The app says I already joined Open My Classes and look for the class. Select its card to view quizzes. If it is not present after refreshing the page, sign out and back in once; then contact the lecturer with the class name.

title: I joined, but cannot find a quiz
text: I joined, but cannot find a quiz Open Class Quizzes , clear a class filter if one is active, and confirm the quiz is live and within its availability window. Draft quizzes are not visible to students. Ask the lecturer whether the quiz has been published and whether your class is enrolled.

title: Face setup and camera
text: Face setup and camera

title: The camera permission was denied
text: The camera permission was denied Open the browser's site settings for Easy2U, allow camera access, return to Face Setup , and select Retry . On a phone, also check the operating system camera permission for the browser.

title: The camera is unavailable or busy
text: The camera is unavailable or busy Close video calls and other apps/tabs using the camera. Check that the device has a working camera, then select Retry . If the browser says the page is not secure or cannot use the camera, open the institution's approved Easy2U address and contact the administrator if the issue continues.

title: Face capture does not progress
text: Face capture does not progress Use a brighter, evenly lit place; position one face in the guide; remove obstructions; and follow the blink and head-turn instruction for each pose. Make sure no other person is in frame. Retry once the on-screen guidance indicates a centered face and suitable lighting.

title: My enrollment says pending review
text: My enrollment says pending review This is a normal review state, not an accusation. Wait for the lecturer or reviewer to complete the check, then revisit Face Setup . If an assessment is due before the review finishes, contact the lecturer and explain that your enrollment is pending. Do not attempt to bypass verification.

title: Face setup succeeded, but the assessment still blocks me
text: Face setup succeeded, but the assessment still blocks me Return to Face Setup and check its current status. A pending review or withdrawn biometric consent can block a face-required assessment. Complete the stated setup/review step. If your status is enrolled and the quiz still blocks you, contact the lecturer with the quiz title and exact message.

title: Class quizzes and results
text: Class quizzes and results

title: The quiz says it is not open yet
text: The quiz says it is not open yet Check the opening time shown on the quiz and try again after it begins. Confirm your device date/time is correct. If the displayed time has passed, ask the lecturer to verify the quiz schedule.

title: The quiz says the window has closed
text: The quiz says the window has closed The availability period has ended. Contact the lecturer to ask whether the quiz can be reopened; students cannot change the window.

title: I already attempted the quiz or cannot retake it
text: I already attempted the quiz or cannot retake it The attempt limit and retake setting are controlled by the lecturer. Return to the quiz card and use Resume , Start , or View results only when that action is shown. Ask the lecturer if you believe the attempt was interrupted or recorded incorrectly.

title: My result says “Awaiting results”
text: My result says “Awaiting results” The quiz was submitted but the lecturer has not released results. Check again later or ask when results will be available. You cannot access hidden scores from the student view before release.

title: I cannot find “View results”
text: I cannot find “View results” Confirm the lecturer has released results and that the quiz card shows the released state. Clear any class filter and verify you are in the correct class. If the quiz remains missing, contact the lecturer.

title: Paused or interrupted assessment
text: Paused or interrupted assessment

title: A pause overlay asks me to verify my face
text: A pause overlay asks me to verify my face Stay on the quiz page, center your face, and follow the blink instruction. Keep the camera available and wait for the recovery control/state. A pause is a recovery state; it does not by itself mean you have been accused of misconduct.

title: The camera stopped during the assessment
text: The camera stopped during the assessment Restore the Easy2U browser camera permission, close any other app using it, and use the retry/recovery action shown on the overlay. Keep the page open. Contact your lecturer if it does not resume.

title: The app says I left the tab or fullscreen
text: The app says I left the tab or fullscreen Return to the quiz tab and accept the fullscreen prompt if shown. Keep the page in the foreground. If the app asks the lecturer to unlock the attempt, contact them with the quiz title and approximate pause time.

title: The page reloaded, browser closed, or connection dropped
text: The page reloaded, browser closed, or connection dropped Reopen Class Quizzes and check whether the card offers a resume action. An answer is not guaranteed saved if the player did not acknowledge it before the interruption. Avoid starting a new attempt unless the card offers it or your lecturer advises you to.

title: Submission failed or the timer expired
text: Submission failed or the timer expired Keep the player open and use an on-screen retry if one appears. Wait for a completion/submission state, then check the quiz card. A timed attempt may submit automatically at expiry. If there is no completion state or the recorded status looks wrong, contact the lecturer promptly with the time and error text.

title: A gesture or focus warning keeps appearing
text: A gesture or focus warning keeps appearing Follow the on-screen instructions and keep your hand/face visible if those checks are enabled. Use a normal answer control only if the interface offers it. If you cannot operate the quiz, contact the lecturer; do not attempt to disable or bypass checks.

title: Personal quizzes and sharing
text: Personal quizzes and sharing

title: I cannot create or edit a personal quiz
text: I cannot create or edit a personal quiz Check required title, prompt, and answer fields, then retry the visible save/add action. AI generation and image options depend on institution configuration. If your quiz is missing from My Quizzes after a refresh, contact support using .

title: A shared quiz link says it is invalid or unavailable
text: A shared quiz link says it is invalid or unavailable Ask the owner for the current link. They may have rotated the code, stopped sharing, or deleted the quiz. A previous link will not work after rotation or revocation. Sign in if prompted, then reopen the current link.

title: A shared quiz stopped working while I was playing
text: A shared quiz stopped working while I was playing The owner may have stopped sharing during your attempt. Ask them for a new link if they intend to share it again. Answers or feedback may no longer be available after access is revoked.

title: Classes and join codes
text: Classes and join codes

title: I created a class, but students cannot join
text: I created a class, but students cannot join Open My Classes and check that the class is active. From its detail page, select Copy join code or Show QR and share the current code or link. An archived class cannot accept new joins. If students see a temporary lockout, they should wait for the displayed interval rather than keep trying codes. Send them the .

title: A student is missing from the roster
text: A student is missing from the roster Confirm that the student joined this class, not another class with a similar name. On a phone, select the Students tab in class detail. If a large class shows a truncation notice, only the first 100 students are listed, but other enrolled students still count toward quizzes and exports. Check the gradebook or contact if the enrollment is disputed.

title: Quiz creation and publishing
text: Quiz creation and publishing

title: Publish quiz is unavailable
text: Publish quiz is unavailable Open the draft in the builder and add at least one valid question. Check each question's prompt, options or rubric, and answer key. A class must be active to accept a new quiz. Review any validation message and retry the visible Publish quiz action.

title: Students cannot see or start a published quiz
text: Students cannot see or start a published quiz Check that the status is Live , the student belongs to the class, and the Opens at and Closes at times permit a start. A live quiz can be scheduled for later or past its closing time. If the class is archived, restore it only after checking whether its live quizzes should reopen.

title: I closed a quiz by mistake
text: I closed a quiz by mistake Closing is one-way. Do not promise students that it can be returned to Live. Review the submitted attempts and results, then use your institution's support route for the next course action. A duplicate creates a fresh draft, but it does not carry student attempts or results.

title: Assessment attempts and face checks
text: Assessment attempts and face checks

title: A student is flagged or cannot resume
text: A student is flagged or cannot resume Open the quiz's Results , find the student's session, and read its status and Integrity timeline . Decide whether Unlock is appropriate. If a camera issue prevents checks, consider Face-exempt for that attempt and record the required reason. Do not Reset unless you intend to permanently delete that attempt's answers, progress and integrity details.

title: Face enrollment needs review
text: Face enrollment needs review On My Classes , inspect the pending enrollment panel. Use your normal identity-check process before selecting Approve or Reject — ask to re-enroll . A rejection asks the student to capture again. If you cannot establish the identity, use rather than guessing.

title: A result is missing or still hidden from students
text: A result is missing or still hidden from students Check that the student's attempt is completed. Inspect Pending or Needs review short answers before releasing marks. On Results , Results are hidden means students cannot yet see scores. Select Reveal to students only when the assessment is ready. An unrevealed marker in the gradebook is expected before release.

title: AI import and export
text: AI import and export

title: Import questions reports a line error
text: Import questions reports a line error Return to Bulk import questions , check the line named in the message, and correct its pipe-separated format and answer marker. Confirm the preview and that the draft has enough of its 30 question slots remaining. Only .txt and .csv files load through this import dialog.

title: AI generation or document scanning fails
text: AI generation or document scanning fails Review the file type and size shown in Generate quiz from file . Check the extracted-content preview before continuing. For scanned material, switch to an available scanner or retry the pages the dialog names. If a generation was cancelled, nothing was saved; if it says questions were saved but the review screen failed, reopen the builder. You can add questions manually while a configured AI service is unavailable.

title: Export Excel fails or appears incomplete
text: Export Excel fails or appears incomplete Check whether you are on the quiz's Results page or the class Gradebook ; they produce different reports. Retry once if the page reports a temporary export error. If a gradebook shows a row, column or session truncation notice, read that notice before interpreting the file. Store any downloaded report in an institution-approved location and use if exports continue to fail.

title: Phone layout
text: Phone layout

title: I cannot see the bottom navigation
text: I cannot see the bottom navigation Close the on-screen keyboard. The bottom dock hides while a text field is active so it does not cover the form. If you are taking an assessment, use the quiz's own navigation controls; the usual app dock is absent in the focused quiz player.

title: The lecturer gradebook looks different on my phone
text: The lecturer gradebook looks different on my phone The desktop gradebook is a student-by-quiz table. On a phone it becomes a student list with a sheet for one student or quiz at a time. Select a student or quiz to inspect its details, then close the sheet to return to the list.

title: A quiz-builder control is missing on my phone
text: A quiz-builder control is missing on my phone Use the builder's add-question control to open its sheet, or expand a question's compact controls. Some actions are under More actions . If a control remains inaccessible after closing the keyboard, report the device, browser, screen width and control name through .

title: Escalation
text: Escalation Contact your lecturer for class membership, quiz schedules, face review, attempt pauses/unlocks, retakes, and result release. Contact your institution's account administrator for sign-in, matric, institutional Microsoft sign-in, or camera/security configuration problems. If neither can resolve an app failure, use the student route in . Include the exact message, quiz/class title, device/browser, and approximate time; never send your password, share code, or face image in a support report.

title: Terms used in this manual
text: Terms used in this manual Term Meaning --- --- Class A lecturer's group of students and its assigned quizzes. Join code / QR A way to enter a class. The lecturer shares the six-character code or displays its QR link. Draft A quiz the lecturer can edit; students cannot start it. Live A published quiz. Opening and closing times may still limit when a student can start. Closed A quiz that no longer accepts new attempts. Closing is one-way. Practice quiz A class quiz with repeat attempts and immediate feedback, or a separate personal quiz made by a student. The guide identifies which kind it means. Assessment A class quiz whose attempt, verification, score release, and possible time limit are controlled by the lecturer's settings. Attempt One student's run through a class quiz. A retake is a new attempt when the lecturer allows one. Face enrollment The student's one-time camera setup for ver

title: Get more help
text: Get more help Internal edition: use your existing class and institution IT channels. Add the actual helpdesk contact and lecturer communication channel before public distribution. First, search . If you are in an active quiz, use .

title: Students
text: Students Contact your lecturer through the class's usual communication channel when the problem involves a join code, a missing class quiz, availability, an assessment pause or flag, a result that has not been released, or permission to retry. Your lecturer can inspect the attempt and decide whether an unlock, face exemption, or reset is appropriate. For account access, institutional Microsoft sign-in, or a matric-number correction, use your institution's account or IT support channel. A lecturer may refer you to that channel if the issue is outside the class.

title: Lecturers
text: Lecturers Use your institution's application or IT support channel for invite-code, account, AI service, camera-service, or repeated export failures. Student attempt actions remain in the quiz's Results page.

title: What to include in a report
text: What to include in a report - Your role (student or lecturer), device type, browser, and whether you used English or Bahasa Melayu. - The class or quiz title, approximate time, and the exact on-screen message. - What you were trying to do and which documented recovery steps you tried. Never send a password, lecturer invite code, matric number, face photo, incident video, or a downloaded gradebook in an ordinary support message. If a screenshot is requested, remove private information before sending it.
